free_tier.stated: The Activate Portfolio tier offers up to USD 200,000 in AWS Activate Credits for provider-backed startups. Eligibility includes: associated with an Activate Provider and have their Organizational ID, not previously received AWS Activate Credits of equal or greater value, Pre-Series B with the most recent funding round in the last 12 months, a fully functioning company website, and founded in the past 10 years.

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
chaining: USD 200,000 of AWS spend would cover a serious training or serving run for a year, and the credits apply to Bedrock third-party models. The chain breaks at the Org ID: it is issued by an investor, so it composes only for a company that has already raised.

limits.value: The Activate Provider Org ID fails first: without a VC or accelerator that is a registered provider, no application can be submitted at all.

identity_cost.detail: Requires an Organizational ID issued by an Activate Provider, which is a VC, accelerator or startup organization. That is an investor relationship, not a document the client can produce alone.

evidence.proved: Portfolio tier offers up to USD 200,000 and requires an Activate Provider Organizational ID plus a funding round in the last 12 months, quoted
the page names Andreessen Horowitz, Brex, Carta, Greylock, Sequoia and Y Combinator as Activate Providers, which is the class of entity that issues the Org ID, quoted

notes: Additional credits above USD 200,000 are stated to exist for AI startups, routed through an AWS account manager, which is a sales conversation rather than a program. The lifetime cap is unnamed on the page.
